issues.description: HAS_PERCENTAGE regex lacks /i flag while HAS_KEYWORD has it, creating undocumented case-sensitivity asymmetry.
issues.detail: In keyframe-selector-notation, HAS_KEYWORD uses /i but HAS_PERCENTAGE does not. Percentages are digit-only so it works today, but the asymmetry signals the data shape wasn't audited. State and verify the invariant that the prefilter is a strict superset of what the walker would flag, or normalize both flags.

issues.description: import-notation url(/string prefilter needs verification against quoted strings containing 'url('.
issues.detail: Under primary='url', the prefilter returns when url( appears anywhere in params. A string parameter containing the literal text 'url(' inside quotes would incorrectly skip the slow path, a correctness risk. Pike notes the gating direction is inverted relative to sibling rules. Add a test case for quoted 'url(' inside string params.

issues.description: font-weight-notation HAS_NAMED/HAS_NUMERIC have inconsistent case-sensitivity and over-match the full shorthand value.
issues.detail: HAS_NAMED is case-insensitive while HAS_NUMERIC is not; the asymmetry is undocumented. Regexes also scan entire decl.value rather than isolating the font-weight token position in the font shorthand. State the invariant that every value the full parser would flag also matches the prefilter, and pick one case stance.

issues.description: selectorRegex = /./ sentinel is clever where a conditional branch would be obvious.
issues.detail: Using /./ as a 'match everything' sentinel to satisfy walkRules' filter signature is the kind of cleverness that hurts the next maintainer. Branch on whether a filter exists and call walkRules with or without it. Same machine code, clearer diff.

issues.description: media-feature-range-notation /(?:min|max)-/i is a loose over-approximation that may match outside feature names.
issues.detail: The pattern matches min-/max- anywhere in atRule.params, including inside calc(), custom properties, or comments. Correctness is preserved since false positives only fall through to the slow path, but the loose invariant deserves a one-line comment noting the regex is a fast over-approximation by design.

issues.description: Performance claim is unmeasured; no before/after numbers in the PR or changeset.
issues.detail: Six rules touched for a perf win, but no benchmark, profile output, or timings appear. Knuth's rule: measure before optimizing. A small benchmark table (microseconds per 10k decls before/after) would confirm this is the critical 3% and establish a budget future refactors must protect.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the patch shape is correct: cheap regex prefilters before expensive parser walks across six *-notation rules, small and scoped. Three concrete concerns recur across reviewers: case-sensitivity asymmetries between paired regexes (HAS_PERCENTAGE vs HAS_KEYWORD, HAS_NAMED vs HAS_NUMERIC) are undocumented and signal an unaudited invariant, and the import-notation url(/string prefilter needs verification against quoted strings containing 'url('. Taste issues — the /./ sentinel and unmeasured perf claim — are minor. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK on the case-asymmetry and import-notation edge case before landing; otherwise the approach is sound.
